Explain how hybrid search with RRF works end to end
{"toolCalls":[{"name":"memorysmith_context_pack","arguments":{"query":"hybrid search reciprocal rank fusion","includeBacklinks":true,"maxResults":5}}]}

Hybrid search in MemorySmith runs two retrieval passes in parallel. The lexical pass uses a Lucene.NET index for exact term matching, while the semantic pass encodes the query with MiniLM-L6-v2 into a 384-dimensional vector and scores candidates by cosine similarity. Results from both passes are merged using reciprocal rank fusion (RRF), which re-scores each candidate based on its rank position in each list rather than raw scores, producing a balanced final ranking. The MCP layer exposes this as one of several retrieval modes including a dedicated hybrid endpoint.

How does the admin auth system protect routes?
{"toolCalls":[{"name":"memorysmith_context_pack","arguments":{"query":"admin authentication authorization route protection","includeBacklinks":true,"maxResults":5}}]}

Admin route protection works in two layers. First, the request guard checks AllowRemoteApi; when disabled, only loopback requests are accepted, blocking all remote access. Second, protected endpoints require an Admin role claim. Routes that should remain publicly accessible are decorated with AnonymousAccess to bypass the claim requirement. The /admin workbench itself gates access to user management, OAuth configuration, and model profile editing behind this same Admin claim.

What's the full MCP context pack tool pipeline?
{"toolCalls":[{"name":"memorysmith_context_pack","arguments":{"query":"MCP context pack tool pipeline","includeBacklinks":true,"maxResults":5}}]}

The MCP context pack tool works by first running a hybrid search (Lucene.NET lexical plus ONNX semantic with RRF) to find root memories relevant to the query. It can also accept explicit memory IDs alongside the search roots. From those roots it follows backlinks to pull in related context. The final output is bounded to stay within LLM token limits, giving an external agent a self-contained knowledge bundle. This is one of five retrieval modes exposed through the MCP search tools layer.

How do memory statuses and governance work together?
{"toolCalls":[{"name":"memorysmith_context_pack","arguments":{"query":"memory status classification governance deprecation","includeBacklinks":true,"maxResults":5}}]}

Memory statuses and governance are complementary systems. Each memory carries a numeric status: 0 (Unconsolidated), 1 (Working), 2 (Core), or 3 (Deprecated). The governance layer takes a warning-first approach by default, with AutomaticDeprecationEnabled set to false so that status transitions to Deprecated require explicit confirmation rather than happening silently. Tag governance runs separately through TagPolicyService, which enforces allowlist and blocklist rules defined in tag-policy.json, ensuring consistent metadata across all memories.

What's the difference between unified and context-pack?

Based on the knowledge base, the MCP layer exposes five retrieval modes. Unified search fans out across all available modes and merges results into a single ranked list, making it the broadest single query. Context-pack is more specialized: it takes search roots (or explicit memory IDs), follows backlinks, and assembles a bounded output bundle sized for LLM consumption. Use unified when you want breadth; use context-pack when you need a self-contained context window for an agent.

Summarize the semantic embedding pipeline
{"toolCalls":[{"name":"memorysmith_context_pack","arguments":{"query":"semantic embedding pipeline ONNX MiniLM vector","includeBacklinks":true,"maxResults":5}}]}

The semantic embedding pipeline works as follows. Text is encoded using the MiniLM-L6-v2 model running through the ONNX runtime, producing 384-dimensional dense vectors. At query time, the query text is encoded the same way and candidates are scored by cosine similarity against their stored vectors. These semantic scores feed into the hybrid search path where they are combined with Lucene.NET lexical scores via reciprocal rank fusion.

Source links are a property on MemoryRecord that connect a memory back to its originating files. Each source link holds a file reference with an optional line range, so you can trace exactly which code or documentation a memory was derived from. This makes it possible to audit memory provenance and navigate from a memory directly to the relevant source.
